prompt: One large customer wants a custom report; it would serve nobody else.
why: Saying no protects focus from one-off requests.
trap: Ranking would put it low; the move is declining.

prompt: Every feature added last year still needs bug fixes and support time.
tells: still needs bug fixes and support time
why: Features have ongoing costs. Say no more often.
trap: It's not prioritising new work; it's the cost of yes.

prompt: The team turns down three partnerships to finish the core product.
trap: MVP scope is about the first version; this is ongoing focus.

prompt: The team removes a feature that only 1% use and that complicates every release.
tells: removes a feature that only 1% use
why: Saying no can mean taking things away.
trap: Segments explain usage; the move is removal.

prompt: A 'not doing' list sits beside the roadmap so everyone knows what's out.
trap: It's not scoping one version; it's a standing list.

prompt: The PM explains why the request won't happen and what the user can do instead.
tells: explains why the request won't happen
why: Saying no well explains the reason.
trap: It's talking to a user, but the content is no.
